newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices wane ahead of U.S. indicators.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices wane ahead of U.S. indicators.

text.p: Danish bond prices edged slightly down in thin trade on Thursday, ahead of U.S. employment data due at 1230 GMT.

At 1150 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.03 point to 110.23, yielding 6.44 percent, in turnover of 725 million crowns. Its June future was down 0.02 point to 109.78, with three contracts traded.

The six percent mortgage bond due 2026, however, rose 0.22 point to 88.50. Credit Suisse First Boston on Thursday recommended Danish mortgage bonds as having higher returns than government bonds at identical currency risk.
The crown traded at 3.8063 per mark, down from Thursday's 3.8055.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 65 basis points.

The Central Bank was less active on the market, selling an estimated 100 million crowns of bonds as part of its routine financing operations, compared to Thursday's 1.7 billion. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969650
